searchText: Attempting to submit a validator deposit, but I keep getting this: ``` ➜ eth ./devnet_deposits.sh USE AT YOUR OWN RISK Are you sure you've double checked the values and want to make this deposit? y Sending deposit for validator "m/12381/3600/0/0/0" "85c256fb6d5cb7ec372396fe3204a8386540f05023c9474d21158403ca92b0eaa39493b5bb4e89fffbcc8ba584e36441" Failed to send deposit: net/http: nil Context Sent deposit for validator "m/12381/3600/0/0/0" "85c256fb6d5cb7ec372396fe3204a8386540f05023c9474d21158403ca92b0eaa39493b5bb4e89fffbcc8ba584e36441" ``` Had the same issue with the downloaded version of ethereal. It worked once I built from source. You can also try to use the pathto the geth.ipc (in startup log) instead of 127.0.0.1 in the script I hit the faucet enough to cover eight validators. Provided that I maintain my validators and promise to properly exit them if I choose to stop running them, is there a particular limit I should restrict myself to? I figured I should ask as a matter of etiquette. I guess it just depends on what you are trying to test or what you need the validators for 🙂 If you are testing some sort of infra, then feel free to onboard as many validators as needed to meaningfully test it. I'm a non-dev validating purely to be a part of the process. I think my only "need" to run more validators would be to increase the chances of getting that sweet proposer cred. 😁 So... eight's probably enough, eh? haha 😄 Considering how few external validators there are currently, you'd definitely have some street cred 🙂 It would be great if you could write down the steps you used to get it up and running, your perspective would definitely be different. Or have a look at some of the other testing scenario's we have in the doc, maybe some seem interesting to you.
